newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes tad lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes tad lower in quiet trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed marginally lower at 26.297 to the dollar against Tuesday's close of 26.296 in a generally quiet session, traders said.
"The peso was wedged within a narrow band. The Central Bank stuck to its selling price of 26.297, giving a firm floor for the market," one trader said.
Done rates were limited to just two rates -- 26.296 and 26.297 for trades to be settled tomorrow.
Trades valued today, which were done mostly in the morning, ranged between 26.291 and 26.293. Total trade dwindled to $102.1 million compared with Tuesday's $156.80 million.
Demand for dollars intensified in the past days after domestic interest rates dropped due to excess peso liquidity.
"Without any good investment outlet, many banks chose to go to the dollar," another trader said.
The parallel market rate was weaker with rates slipping to 26.348 from 26.345 in the morning.
"With the Central Bank setting a floor, the peso will remain at the current level," he added.
Another said the continued dollar inflows from Filipino overseas contract workers would provide dampener to a protracted peso depreciation mode.
